chief_complaint: chronic nasal obstruction and external crooked nose with dorsal deviation after facial sports injury
hpi_details: 29M post-boxing trauma presenting with severe S-shaped septal deviation blocking the right nasal airway and dorsal deviation undergoing functional septorhinoplasty using autologous spreader grafts.
ideas: He thinks his nasal cartilage broke and healed crooked after taking a hard punch in boxing sparring, completely walling off the right airway.
concerns: He is worried that mouth-breathing and broken sleep are ruining his athletic stamina and fears that surgery will leave him with an unnatural, artificial-looking nose.
expectations: He hopes to schedule a corrective procedure that straightens his crooked bridge and unblocks his right airway so he can breathe normally through both sides.

reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Rhinoplasty Nasal Septal Deviation.
reference_soap.plan: Perform nasal and septal examination, including screening for septal hematoma and associated facial injury. Urgently assess clear watery rhinorrhea, visual symptoms, or neurologic symptoms after trauma. If persistent obstruction is confirmed after healing, discuss clinician-performed functional septoplasty or septorhinoplasty, with individualized perioperative review of blood pressure and medicines.

history.answer: My nose has been visibly crooked and constantly blocked on the right side ever since I took a punch during a boxing match.
It happened during a boxing sparring session about six months ago, and the blockage and deformity have been present ever since.
The initial bruising and swelling went away after two weeks, but the crooked appearance and blocked breathing haven't improved at all.
No, I don't have any thick, yellow, green, or foul-smelling drainage from my nose.
The obstruction is almost entirely on the right side; air barely moves through it, and it never alternates or clears up.
I had a brief nosebleed right after the blow that stopped quickly, but I haven't had nosebleeds since, and my face does not feel numb.
No, I don't have sneezing fits, itchy eyes, itchy nose, or watery eyes.
The blockage is the same every day, whether it's morning or night, and exposure to dust, pollen, pets, or cold air makes no difference.
No, I don't feel any pain or pressure in my cheeks, forehead, or upper teeth, even when bending forward.
My smell is slightly weaker on the right side just because no air gets up there, but I can still smell normally through the left.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
My vision is completely normal, with no blurriness, double vision, swelling around my eyes, or severe headaches.
I have to breathe through my mouth quite a bit and my girlfriend says I snore now, but I don't gasp or stop breathing in my sleep.
No, I don't feel mucus dripping down the back of my throat, and I don't have a cough or wheezing.
I used an over-the-counter decongestant spray for three days right after the trauma, but it didn't help much, and I haven't used any sprays since.
I don't have asthma, and taking pain medicines like aspirin or ibuprofen has never caused breathing trouble or made my nose worse.
I took a hard direct punch to the nose during boxing six months ago, but I have never had clear water-like fluid leaking from my nose.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 126/82 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, well-developed male in no acute distress, with visible external dorsal deviation of the nasal bridge and cartilaginous framework to the right side.

Anterior rhinoscopy reveals marked S-shaped septal deviation severely obstructing the right nasal airway, no septal hematoma, boggy swelling, mucosal ulcerations, or polyps, with normal oropharynx and no postnasal drainage.
No tenderness on palpation or percussion over the bilateral maxillary and frontal sinuses.
Extraocular movements fully intact without nystagmus or diplopia, visual acuity intact, and no periorbital edema, ecchymosis, or telecanthus.
Facial sensation intact bilaterally across V1, V2, and V3 distributions, with symmetric facial movements and no cranial nerve deficits.
No cervical, submandibular, or preauricular lymphadenopathy noted on palpation.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal vesicular breath sounds and no wheezes, rhonchi, or rales.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2 sounds, and no audible murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
